subject: Acme - SLO/SLA language & performance follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate you walking through Acme's expected traffic and SL roadmap. Short recap and proposed next steps so we can align on SLO language and any redlines for the contract: 

1) Requirements you shared
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end (app → model first token) of <= 250 ms for single-turn inference; streaming for multi-token responses with first-byte p95 <= 250 ms and sustained per-token tail latencies under 50 ms.
- Throughput: baseline 500 qps with ability to burst to 800 qps for short windows.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent request set is ~200 during peak, with spikes to 600 for short events.
- Availability/uptime: target 99.9% for the inference API.

2) What we need from you to finalize draft SLO/SLA language
- Confirmation that the p95 definition above (first-byte measured at Redwood edge from request accepted to first token) is acceptable.
- Expected reporting cadence (monthly preferred) and recipient list for automated SLO reports.
- Any procurement/legal constraints around remedies (service credits vs termination rights).
- Expected test traffic profile or a sample payload for verification (if you can share a small representative set).

3) Next steps
- I will share a first-pass SLO/SLA draft that maps your targets to measurement windows, exclusions, and remedies. (Attached.)
- Aditya (cc'd) will follow up on streaming and batching knobs to ensure we can meet the first-byte and per-token tail numbers at your concurrency.
- Can we lock a 30-min follow-up on Monday to review the SLO wording and any legal asks?

Attached: Acme_SLO_draft_v1.pdf — includes proposed SLO definitions, measurement points, and a sample reporting cadence.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182
[Attachment: Acme_SLO_draft_v1.pdf]
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Thanks Marissa — that summary is spot on. A few clarifications from our side before the Monday call: 

- Measurement point: we prefer the p95 to be measured from our edge (our service accepting the request) to first token delivered to the client. We understand Redwood measures at its edge; can you confirm the measurement delta and whether you can support a customer-side reference measurement for cross-checks?

- Exclusions: planned maintenance windows okay. Also want to exclude degraded performance due to our upstream payload issues (e.g., malformed requests causing retries). We'll propose language — would prefer it to be explicit in the SLA.

- Remedies: Acme's procurement prefers an escalating service credit schedule rather than termination rights for the first year. Typical request: 5% credit for monthly availability below target but above 99.0%, 10% below 99.0% and above 98.0%, and 25% below 98.0%. Are you able to mirror a schedule like that?

- Reporting cadence: monthly automated report delivered to sla-reports@acme.com with a dashboard link. Also request a quarterly technical review with your SE team.

Finally, for verification, we'll share a small set of representative payloads (anonymized) by EOD Friday.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the draft wording.

Alex Turner
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
alex.turner@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Alex — thanks, that's helpful. A few notes inline and high-level answers: 

- Measurement point: Redwood reports p95 measured at the Redwood ingress gateway (time request accepted by Redwood to first token emitted from our runtime). We can include a customer-side measurement clause and a reconciliation process in the SLA: both sides publish measurements and provide a 10-business-day window to reconcile differences with joint logs. We'll add that language to the draft.

- Exclusions: agree on excluding planned maintenance (we'll list scheduled maintenance with >48 hour notice) and recognizable customer-originating faults (backoff loops, malformed payloads). We'll add a short appendix for example exclusions.

- Remedies: we can accept an escalating credit schedule similar to what you proposed. Draft language in the attached maps your tiers to service credit percentages and caps (capped at 50% of monthly invoice). If procurement needs language tweaks we can iterate.

- Reporting cadence / recipients: we'll set up automated monthly SLO reports to sla-reports@acme.com and share a dashboard link. We also propose a dedicated quarterly technical review with Aditya + our reliability team.

- Next steps: please send the anonymized payloads. After we validate against our staging infra, we'll run a short 24–48 hour load test to confirm latency/throughput at your concurrency profile and share results ahead of the Monday sync.

Thanks — attaching updated SLO draft that incorporates the measurement reconciliation and remedies section.

Marissa
[Attachment: Acme_SLO_draft_v1.pdf]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps (technical notes)

Alex / Priya — quick technical clarifications from our end ahead of the load validation: 

- Streaming first-byte: to meet p95 first-byte <= 250 ms we measure from request acceptance to the first token emitted from runtime. For streaming scenarios where you open a long-lived SSE/WebSocket connection, we recommend a small initial batch size (1–4 tokens) to guarantee a low first-byte latency while using larger internal token batches for throughput.

- Concurrency & batching: at 200 concurrent callers with 500 qps, we'll likely use dynamic batching with a 10–30 ms batch window — this typically preserves p95 while improving throughput. For the 600-concurrency spikes, please confirm if those are sustained >5 minutes or short bursts; sustained high concurrency will require reserved capacity (Dedicated) to keep SLOs.

- Cache/KV behavior: if you use repeated prefixes or session-state (KV cache), hit rate will materially reduce per-token latency and cost. Please indicate whether you plan to use session affinity or stateless calls — we'll add recommended caching configs to the test plan.

I'll include these details in the test plan and schedule a 24–48 hour run once you provide payloads. If you're comfortable, we can also run a short streaming-focused test to validate first-byte plus per-token tail latencies.

—Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
